programmes.d: Parsley Smith, a teller of tall tales, claims the new town banker is plotting to make off with the depositors' money.

It's Christmas in Dodge and Chester isn't pleased when his brother Magnus arrives for a visit (Robert Easton appears). One of very few times a radio episode was adapted to TV with the same guest actor playing the role in both media.
A beautiful young wife (Lola Albright) manipulates a young hired hand into killing her older husband.
A peddler's miracle curative contains opium and proves fatal.
A man who claims he's innocent of a murder in a corrupt town breaks out of Matt's jail, and his trail leads Matt to the corrupt sheriff (Mort Mills appears).
A woman offers a $1,000 reward to the man who kills Matt Dillon.
Witnesses are refusing to testify against an infamous outlaw.
Matt saves the life of a white boy raised by Indians who was shot trying to retrieve horses stolen from his tribe.
An ex-lawman and old friend of Matt's arrives in Dodge with failing eyesight, and a man who wants to kill him.
A well-liked hardware drummer is actually a man wanted for multiple murders.
This ambitious frontier epic features a lawman (Kris Kristofferson) and a hitman (Christopher Walken) who fight in a tragic class war between ranchers and starving immigrants.
Matt attempts to reform a young troublemaker (including James Nusser in a role other than Louie Pheeters).
An old rancher decides that he is going to marry Kitty.
When an old Indian scout murders a man, Matt pursues him into Comanche territory.
Doc must find a way to thwart a typhoid epidemic in Dodge.
Matt has to figure a way around a six-foot-tall, 200-pound woman with a six-gun.
An old friend of Matt's is now a gun-for-hire, in town to kill him. This is the actual pilot episode of the television Gunsmoke.
A dishonest gambler uses a mentally challenged man in a plot against Matt.
Matt has to stop a cold-blooded killer who preys on over-matched opponents.
Doc has a change of heart about a man he hates and wants to kill face to face when the man is later shot in the back.
A preacher disgusted by violence is harassed by bully Sam Keeler who despises his timid nature.
The brother of a man Matt was forced to kill vows to kill Matt by any means necessary.
Matt is forced to arrest his childhood hero, who is now the leader of a gang of horse thieves.
A bitter old man tells fibs about Indians preparing to strike Dodge.
When Chester's mail-order bride arrives, neither she nor Chester are what the other are expecting.
An ex-Union soldier is forced to use violence against a pair of diehard Rebels.
Matt discovers that an old girlfriend is working on the opposite side of the law.
A self-described religious prophet makes life miserable for his sister and her husband.
An old woman grieving over the loss of her outlaw son tries to help another young outlaw escape justice. Boot Hill Intro returns for this episode and appears intermittently hereafter.
Homesteaders are ambushed on the way to Dodge.
A wounded Doc may be forced to save the life of the man who wounded him.
Matt tracks a murderer to a strange town where the people are unwilling to cooperate.
Matt refuses to turn in a rustler for a court-martial. Boot Hill intro clearly shows grave markers with dates of 1882 & 1883, yet episode is set in 1876, the year of the Battle of the Little Bighorn.
Dodge City merchants celebrate the end of a round-up and unite against any acts of violence.
The brother of an outlaw Matt killed swears revenge.
A white boy who has been raised by Indians learns to live with his own race.
Matt is used by an old friend in a con game.
Doc comes upon a homesteader with a busted leg and a gun to protect himself from his wife.
Matt leaves Dodge City unprotected when he sets out to find a killer.
An outlaw threatens to kill Doc if he does not help his wounded buddy.
Matt and Chester act as decoys to ambush outlaws that are masking their crimes as those of renegade Indians.
